# JsonLimits

What a caller will accept from a document.

```rux
pub struct JsonLimits {
    pub maximumBytes: uint;
    pub maximumTextBytes: uint;
    pub maximumDepth: uint;
    pub maximumEntries: uint;
}
```

Every field is a refusal a caller might need to make against untrusted input, and every default is generous
enough for ordinary documents and far short of what exhausts a machine.

## Fields

| Name               | Type   | Description                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `maximumBytes`     | `uint` | The longest document, in bytes.                                                           |
| `maximumTextBytes` | `uint` | The longest single string, in bytes.                                                      |
| `maximumDepth`     | `uint` | How deeply containers may nest. This is the one that protects a recursive parser's stack. |
| `maximumEntries`   | `uint` | How many elements or members one container may hold.                                      |

## Associated functions

<h3 id="default"><code>Default</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Default() -> JsonLimits
```

Limits generous enough for ordinary documents: sixty-four mebibytes, sixteen mebibyte strings, a hundred
and twenty-eight levels of nesting, and a million entries per container.

**Returns**: the limits an ordinary parse uses

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Json/Src/Lexer.rux#L94)

<h3 id="unlimited"><code>Unlimited</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Unlimited() -> JsonLimits
```

No limits at all, for input that is already trusted.
Named so that choosing it is visible: a document read from the network should never use this, and a
reviewer should be able to find every place that did.

**Returns**: limits that refuse nothing, for input that is already trusted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Json/Src/Lexer.rux#L108)
